page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom 64-bit ARM architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 processor family running at 2.5 GHz, with no hyperthreading, resulting in exactly one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and a massive 15,000 GB local NVMe SSD storage array. Network connectivity is supported by a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate balanced performance across standard operations, though single-threaded execution presents a relative bottleneck. The instance achieves average ratings in multi-core processing, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48,576.94 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,490.0. Memory bandwidth is strong for cached small blocks at 1,893.97 GB/sec, but drops to 162.83 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Tradeoffs are evident in single-threaded tasks, where the instance registers weak performance in Geekbench single-core (941.0) and poor performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression (7.01 GB/sec). LLM inference tasks also show weak to poor performance on smaller models, though medium 7B model processing remains average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the im4gn.8xlarge offers high resource density by combining an efficient ARM64 architecture with an exceptionally large local NVMe SSD capacity. This makes it highly suitable for storage-intensive workloads that require high IOPS and substantial local caching without the overhead of external network storage. Recommended workloads include database operations, which are supported by a Passmark database score of 20,399.25 and 38.19 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks, as well as static web serving and multi-threaded data processing.
